text: The brownie is a Scottish and British folkloric figure. Feminist Juliette Gordon Low recalled such spirits. She named the youngest girls of her Scouts after them. The brownie is a friendly fairy that stays close to the home. Some evidence says the brownie is a late development. It may have no roots in the Celtic worldview. It could arise from disguised ancestor worship. The special brownie called the Gruagach seems divine. It lives in the Hebrides. People poured milk over stones it held sacred. Those gifts kept it guarding the herds. Most observers called the brownie a stout hairy man. Others said that although short, it was not rotund. Its hair was fair and flowing. It wore ragged brown clothes. It was typically male. The brownie did barn work at night. It threshed, tidied, and curried horses. It also helped in sheepherding and mowing. It could serve as a confidante and adviser. No one should fuss over its needs. No one should offer it a suit of clothes. Such a gift made the brownie leave. In Cornwall the boggart is its trickster version.

okr.objective: Describe the brownie as a helpful household spirit and its rules of conduct.
